name: Test Driven Development Best Practices
description: This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building test driven development — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary test driven development tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.
content:
This module lists the best, most commonly recommended practices for writing, implementing, and building test driven development — the default, everyday guidance to apply on typical, ordinary test driven development tasks and implementations, not specialized or unusual ones.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple test driven development strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Prefer explicit, readable test driven development solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Keep test driven development changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to test driven development (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Check that test driven development terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
6. Prefer the simplest test driven development approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Keep test driven development outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Measure before optimizing any test driven development bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated test driven development concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop test driven development edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of test driven development correctness.
- Do not apply generic test driven development advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new test driven development abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about test driven development over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
